comparator.name: Actuarial Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The Dutch and English tracks share the same curriculum. Each of the first two years has ten 6 EC courses. The third year pairs 30 EC of electives or approved experiential study with five 6 EC components, including the research and skills components of the thesis.
components: Research Seminar Actuarial Science and Mathematical Finance
Choose electives, a minor, study abroad, or an internship combined with electives.
Bachelor’s Thesis Seminar Actuarial Science – Research Project
Bachelor’s Thesis Seminar Actuarial Science – Skills

core: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and mathematical economic prediction
Probability, statistics and econometric analysis of uncertain events
Finance, insurance, pensions and the financial impact of risk
Data science, programming and quantitative decision support
Actuarial risk models, life contingencies and reserving
Responsible modelling, sustainability and the social consequences of risk decisions
adjacent: Financial economics and quantitative risk management
questions: How can probability, statistics and economic models quantify uncertain future losses?
How should organisations use data and models to make responsible risk decisions?

uses strategic analysis and planning to evaluate responsible responses to digital change

develops advanced microeconomic analysis of choice under uncertainty, firms and markets

uses regression and classification, regularisation and resampling to build and evaluate predictions

alternatives.label: Finance, economics & quantitative risk
alternatives.labelReason: Finance and economics provide the applications, and probability, numerical methods, econometrics and predictive modelling provide the analytical tools. UCR’s risk examples are drawn from markets, banks and economic decisions.
alternatives.concept: Build a foundation in economics, calculus, probability and programming. Then use econometrics and machine learning to model uncertainty, study asset pricing and bank risk, and test how decisions change when assumptions change.
progression: Calculus and programming precede probability and computational modelling. Linear algebra and data exploration precede machine learning, and statistical research methods precede econometrics. The plan develops financial and economic applications alongside the mathematical work.

selection.assessment: One option integrates the quantitative and financial strands. An insurance and pensions direction lacks courses in pricing, reserving and life-contingency models. A more computational variant would replace economic and financial applications with general algorithms or machine learning, weakening its response to actuarial risk. A broader policy route would similarly dilute the quantitative-financial spine. These variants do not justify an additional option.

blocks: Both develop differential and integral calculus. UCR also introduces differential equations.
Both study matrices, linear systems and vector spaces.
Both extend calculus to problems with several variables. UvA emphasises nonlinear analysis, including numerical methods.
Both study multivariate probability and statistical inference. UvA develops these topics over several courses.
Both develop descriptive statistics. UvA also teaches probability theory as a foundation for its later courses.
UvA continues linear algebra with orthogonalisation, matrix decompositions and optimisation.
UvA develops advanced statistical theory, including convergence and properties of tests.
Both introduce consumer choice, firms and markets. UCR also teaches introductory macroeconomics.
Both use macroeconomic models to study growth, inflation and economic policy. UCR also studies open economies.
Both study choice under uncertainty, firm behaviour and market equilibrium. UvA uses more multivariate analysis.
Both introduce investment and financing decisions. UCR also devotes substantial attention to accounting.
Both study financial instruments and financial risk. UCR also focuses on banks and monetary institutions.
Both develop programming and algorithmic thinking. UvA also teaches numerical analysis in this course.
Both prepare and explore data before modelling.
Both build and evaluate models for predicting outcomes. UvA applies these ideas to quantitative economics.
Both use multiple regression to study relationships between economic variables. UvA continues the sequence in a second course.
UvA extends regression and the interpretation of quantitative results in a second econometrics course.
UvA studies recent developments in actuarial science and mathematical finance in a dedicated seminar.
UvA introduces econometrics and actuarial problems together through an applied research project.
UvA models the pricing and reserving of life insurance and pensions.
UvA teaches a dedicated actuarial risk theory course.
UvA sets aside 30 EC for electives, a minor, study abroad or an internship with electives.
UvA teaches accounting in the specific context of life insurers.
UvA applies stochastic models to life insurance.
UvA requires a 6 EC thesis research project. Optional UCR research is separate from the illustrated schedule.
UvA separately assigns 6 EC to actuarial thesis skills.

notes.text: UvA teaches life-insurance pricing, pension valuation and reserving, insurance accounting and stochastic insurance models. The UCR option studies related quantitative and financial methods. Its schedule has no dedicated insurance or pension sequence or actuarial thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Actuarial Science at the University of Amsterdam uses mathematics, statistics and data to estimate financial risks, particularly in insurance and pensions.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option combines economics and finance with methods for analysing uncertainty. It includes investment and banking examples, while UvA applies its methods to insurance and pensions.
